segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus spoke to them again:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in the darkness but will have the light of life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are testifying about yourself; your testimony is not true.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Even if I do testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You judge by human standards; I judge no one.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet even if I do judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone; it is I and the Father who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And in your own law it is written that the testimony of two people is true.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where is your father?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father as well.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He spoke these words in the treasury while teaching in the temple, and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he said to them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely he is not going to kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: That is why I told you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who are you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why am I speaking to you at all?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the one who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him is what I speak to the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but speak these things just as the Father taught me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the one who sent me is with me. He has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was saying these things, many believed in him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We are Abraham’s descendants and have never been slaves to anyone. How can you say, ‘You will become free’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The slave does not remain in the household forever; the son remains forever.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will really be free.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know that you are Abraham’s descendants. Yet you are seeking to kill me, because my word finds no room in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I speak of what I have seen in the Father’s presence; and you, then, do what you have heard from your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Our father is Abraham.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you are Abraham’s children, you would be doing the works of Abraham.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are doing the works of your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father: God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came out from God and am here. I have not come on my own; he sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Why do you not understand the way I speak? Because you cannot hear my word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are from your father the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks from what is his own, because he is a liar and the father of lies.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Which of you can convict me of sin? If I am telling the truth, why do you not believe me?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever is from God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you are not from God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I do not have a demon. I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and who judges.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you: if anyone keeps my word, they will never see death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet you say, ‘If anyone keeps my word, they will never taste death.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Surely you are not greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died too. Who do you make yourself out to be?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, the one of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet you have not come to know him, but I know him. If I said that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I keep his word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Your father Abraham was overjoyed that he would see my day; he saw it and was glad.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you: before Abraham came to be, I am.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.

notes.phrase: Then Jesus spoke to them again
notes.note: The story of the woman caught in adultery (7:53–8:11) is not printed here. It is absent from the earliest surviving manuscripts of John and appears at different places in later ones, and the SBLGNT edition translated here does not include it in the main text. Most scholars regard it as an early tradition about Jesus that was not originally part of this Gospel, so verse 12 continues the temple scene of chapter 7.

The setting is still the Feast of Tabernacles (7:2, 14, 37). Later rabbinic tradition describes great lamps lit in the temple courts during this festival, and many interpreters think the saying alludes to them. The image of God as his people's light is also common in the Scriptures (for example Psalm 27:1; Isaiah 60:19).

The Greek is literally 'according to the flesh', which formal versions keep. Here 'flesh' means the merely human vantage point, judging by what can be seen, not the body or sinful desire, and a modern reader is likely to hear one of those other senses. Several modern versions render the phrase in the same way as here.

notes.phrase: the testimony of two people is true
notes.note: The reference is to the rule in Deuteronomy 17:6 and 19:15 that a matter must be established by two or three witnesses. Jesus paraphrases the rule and does not quote it word for word. He then applies it by naming himself and the Father as the two witnesses.

The Greek says only 'I am', with nothing following. In ordinary speech the phrase can mean 'I am he' or 'it is I', which is why the hearers ask 'Who are you?'. Used without a complement it also echoes God's self-declaration in the Greek version of Isaiah (for example Isaiah 43:10, 'that you may know and believe that I am he'). The same phrase recurs in verse 28 and, with unmistakable force, in verse 58; some translations render all three simply as 'I am'.

notes.phrase: Why am I speaking to you at all?
notes.traditional: Just what I have been telling you from the beginning
notes.note: This is one of the most obscure sentences in John, and its meaning is disputed. Most English versions take it as a statement: '(I am) what I have been telling you from the beginning'. The rendering here follows the punctuation of the edition translated, which reads it as a question, and takes the opening phrase in its common adverbial sense 'at all'; this reading is also found among early Greek-speaking interpreters. A third option is an exclamation: 'That I speak to you at all!'

In John this verb carries a deliberate double sense: being raised up on the cross and being exalted (see 3:14; 12:32–34). The same verb is used of the exaltation of the Lord's servant in the Greek version of Isaiah 52:13.

notes.phrase: do what you have heard from your father
notes.note: In the text translated here neither 'father' has 'my' or 'your', and the verb can be a statement ('you do') or a command ('do'). The alternative reading is an appeal: 'so you too should do what you have heard from the Father'. The rendering here takes the sentence as the first hint of the contrast between two fathers that becomes explicit in verses 41 and 44, which is how the reply in verse 39 seems to understand it. Many later manuscripts add the pronouns to make this sense explicit.

The Greek word covers unlawful sexual relations of any kind; many modern versions paraphrase as 'We are not illegitimate children'. In the prophets the same word is a standard image for Israel's unfaithfulness to God through idolatry (Hosea 1:2; 2:4), which fits the claim that follows, to have God alone as Father. Some interpreters also hear a slur on the circumstances of Jesus's own birth, but that is uncertain.

notes.phrase: You are from your father the devil
notes.note: The words are addressed to a particular group of hearers in this scene, whom Jesus accuses of seeking his death (verses 37, 40). The dispute is among Jews: Jesus and his earliest followers were themselves Jewish. The argument turns on likeness of conduct, not ancestry (verse 39), and such sharp language about parentage is found in other Jewish polemic of the period. The verse has a long history of being used against Jewish people as a whole, which the context does not support.

notes.phrase: before Abraham came to be, I am
notes.note: The Greek contrasts two verbs: Abraham 'came into being' (that is, was born), while Jesus simply 'is'. The traditional 'before Abraham was' blurs that contrast. The unqualified 'I am' echoes God's self-declarations in the Greek version of Isaiah, and many interpreters also hear Exodus 3:14. The attempt at stoning in the next verse shows the hearers took it as a claim no mere human could make.

candidates.reason: Recurs across John and Paul with senses ranging from body to human nature to the merely human viewpoint, and translators split between 'flesh' and paraphrase.
A key Johannine term (John 15, 1 John) where translations vary between 'abide', 'remain', 'continue' and 'stay', obscuring the thread.
Translations vary between 'slave', 'servant' and 'bondservant' across the Gospels and Paul's self-descriptions, and the choice changes how readers hear the metaphor.

candidates.rendering: Truly, truly, I tell you (for doubled ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν)
candidates.reason: The formula occurs dozens of times in the Gospels, single in the Synoptics and doubled in John, and needs one fixed English form.
The absolute use recurs in John (6:20; 13:19; 18:5–8) and the Synoptics, and needs one consistent policy between 'I am', 'I am he' and 'it is I'.
